text: Pan-Atlantic University is a private, non-profit educational institution located in Lekki, Lagos State. It originated as the Lagos Business School (LBS), established in 1991. The federal government approved it as Pan-African University in 2002, and LBS became its first school. The Ajah Campus was completed in 2003, and work on the Ibeju-Lekki campus began in 2010. The School of Media and Communication (SMC) was approved in 2006 by the Pan-Atlantic University Council, evolving directly from the Centre for Media and Communication, in recognition of the sector's role in shaping societal values and cultural life. In September 2011, the university launched the Virtual Museum of Modern Nigerian Art, a website created by Spanish architect Jess Castellote, featuring over 400 works from 81 artists, including pioneering figures such as Aina Onabolu and Bruce Onobrakpeya, and emerging artists like Richardson Ovbiebo and Babalola Lawson. In November and December 2011, the University's Enterprise Development Centre (EDC) marked the Global Entrepreneurship Week (GEW) in Lagos for the first time, with a series of events that were extremely well-attended, and since then, the EDC has been the designated host of GEW in Nigeria. The EDC collaborates with the Small and Medium Enterprise (SME) Department of the International Finance Corporation (IFC) to provide the SME Toolkit Nigeria, offering free business management information and training to small businesses. In July 2011, British Prime Minister David Cameron delivered a speech at the university in Lagos, discussing aid, trade, and democracy, advocating for an African free trade area and increased trade with Britain. In May 2013, the university's name was changed to Pan-Atlantic University to avoid confusion with the Pan-African University of the African Union. On 17 November 2014, the university launched its first undergraduate programmes at its new Ibeju-Lekki campus. On 19 October 2019, the university's Art museum, the Yemisi Shyllon Museum of Art, officially opened to the public with two simultaneous inaugural exhibitions. Pan-Atlantic University partnered with an environmental sustainability organization to plant trees across its campuses and with the Mastercard Foundation to train ten thousand women in business and vocational training. In February 2024, Pan-Atlantic University was ranked 54th in Nigeria.
